A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SWE-rebench V2. Their main text, tables, figures, and appendices A-C support reliable comparison despite pagination changes and table renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original construction yields, setup and filtering ablations, and seven-model evaluation on 300 tasks, including uncertainty estimates in Appendix C.1.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds a PR-statement leakage audit, diagnostic-category comparisons, and further construction statistics.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 adds an explicit acceptance rule requiring unchanged structured test outcomes across three validation runs, represented as an additional filtering stage in Table 1. This changes the reported validation procedure; setup synthesis, annotation components, and appendix prompts remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish a change in released task membership.

E1.justification: Section 3.6 newly evaluates generated statements for 509 SWE-bench Pro-derived tasks against reference descriptions, requirements, and interfaces. This adds coverage for reference-based leakage assessment. The released corpus retains its 20-language scope; additional language rows in Appendix A.1 describe existing coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons in Tables 2-6 retain the same methods, models, prompts, and ensembles. New Table 7 uses five previously evaluated models for a separate diagnostic-subset analysis; it does not replace the original seven-model comparison.

E3.justification: V2 adds an LLM-based leakage evaluation protocol and an A/B* comparison described as sampling 60 tasks with similar language, modified-file, and modified-line distributions. The allocation between categories is unclear. Existing setup and solver evaluations retain their settings; the baseline clarification in Section 4.1 does not establish a changed experiment.

E4.justification: Two focused analyses are added: auditing solution leakage in generated PR statements and testing whether diagnostic A/B* labels separate tasks with different solve rates. Appendix A.1 also expands the existing filtering-yield breakdown. Original setup, prompt, model, and ensemble ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Section 3.3 first reports three candidate-task validation runs and an outcome-consistency requirement; v1 specifies no repetition count for that check. This does not establish an increase from a previously stated count. The ten setup runs, three solver runs, and Appendix C.1 uncertainty estimates remain unchanged.

E6.justification: V2 reports 23.0% statement leakage, including 2.4% explicit solution leakage, and new A/B* results, such as Gemini pass@3 of 34.0% versus 4.0%. Table 1 changes the issue-filtering count to 33,049 tasks and 3,701 repositories, retaining 32,079 and 3,617 after stability filtering. Appendix A.1 adds language-specific yields. Tables 2-6 and Appendix C.1 retain their scores.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results or proofs, and v2 adds no substantive mathematical definitions, assumptions, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about automated multilingual construction, the two released collections, and diagnostic metadata. Exact counts replace rounded counts already supported in v1; the stability emphasis elaborates the existing reproducibility claim.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly characterizes PR-derived tasks as lower-confidence, interprets the A/B* gap as supporting metadata utility, and adds setup-failure explanations and dependency-drift limitations. Section 5 reframes the existing missing-training-ablation limitation around end-to-end RL and distinguishes prerequisite task checks from demonstrated training benefits.

D1.justification: Section 3.7 newly discloses API calls, token usage, estimated setup costs, Docker build time, and 26.36 TiB of artifacts. V2 also clarifies baseline controls and credential scanning, while removing the TractoAI storage/compute attribution. Appendix recipes and prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited research and substantive related-work positioning remain unchanged. SWE-bench Pro was already discussed in v1; its new experimental use does not introduce a new positioning claim. Bibliographic URL formatting changes are presentational.

P1.justification: V2 adds targeted explanatory paragraphs, revises the limitations discussion, introduces an Impact Statement, and updates acknowledgements and the publication footer. The overall section structure and most prose, including appendix prompts, are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 7, adds a stability row to Table 1, and expands the repository-filtering table from six to nineteen languages with reordered rows and abbreviated headings. Existing tables and appendix material reflow, while both figures and Appendix C.1 displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 provides useful additional evidence about stability, statement leakage, and diagnostic-label utility, alongside clearer construction costs and maintenance limitations. These targeted additions strengthen the paper's support for dataset usability. Their impact remains limited by brief reporting of the new studies, including an unnamed leakage judge and unclear A/B* sample allocation; downstream RL benefits remain untested.
